subject: Nimbus Health — continuous batching & $/1M token target
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@nimbushealth.com>, Tom Bradford <tom.bradford@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus Health — continuous batching & $/1M token target

Hi Aisha / Tom — thanks again for the quick sync today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can turn the call into a pricing/PO conversation: 

Call highlights:
- Primary workload: patient-facing summarization + physician note-generation (mixture of short prompts ~20–120 tokens and long-context summarization up to ~8k tokens).
- Traffic pattern: predictable business hours M–F with two traffic peaks (09:00 and 17:00 PT), plus asynchronous batch jobs overnight for summarization.
- Quality target: match current in-house model qualitatively; tolerance for 1–2% degradation on summaries during night batch windows in exchange for cost wins.

Asks (please reply with the items in bold):
1) Monthly token expectations: can you confirm a realistic range for month 1 / month 3 / month 6 (best guess is fine). We need min/typical/max daily tokens and monthly aggregate. **Please attach a sample CSV of daily token counts if available.**
2) Target unit economics: you mentioned targeting ~$500–$800 per 1M tokens. Please confirm the single-number target or a band you want us to price to.
3) Batching & concurrency expectations: are you comfortable with continuous batching as the primary mode (we’ll auto-aggregate requests into rolling micro-batches to push down $/token) and a concurrency target of ~50–150 concurrent streams during peaks? Any hard latency SLOs (p95/p99) we should bake into the quote?
4) Security/compliance must-haves for Private/Dedicated (if relevant): SOC2 + contract language checklist — any non-standard asks?

Attachments I’m sending: a short estimator (redwood-quant-profiles.pdf) showing quantization and batching tradeoffs plus a sample MAP template.

Next steps: if you can send the CSV and confirm the $/1M target this week, I’ll put together two pricing options (1) continuous-batching-optimized hosted plan and (2) Reserved Dedicated + throughput guarantee with lower unit price.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@nimbushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Bradford <tom.bradford@nimbushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus Health — continuous batching & $/1M token target

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) Monthly token expectations
We ran a quick export and attached a conservative estimate (MAP-token-estimates.xlsx) and a raw usage sample (nimbus-map-usage.csv). Rough monthly buckets:
- Month 1 (pilot): 40M–80M tokens
- Month 3 (ramp): 200M–450M tokens
- Month 6 (production): 800M–1.6B tokens

> 2) Target unit economics
We are targeting ~$600 per 1M tokens as a baseline for procurement approvals; if you can demonstrate reliable 10–20% cost savings with Dedicated/reserved options that would be compelling.

> 3) Batching & concurrency expectations
Continuous batching is fine — our primary constraint is p99 latency for API-backed UX flows: goal is <1.5s p99 for short flows (~<256 tokens). For long-form summarization we can accept higher tail latency overnight. Peak concurrency estimate: 120 concurrent streaming sessions during business peak.

> 4) Security/compliance
SOC2 is required; we’ll send a standard questionnaire next week. No unusual legal asks at this stage.

Attaching the two files now. Let me know if you need a sanitized export or more granular hour-by-hour traffic.

Thanks — Aisha

Attachments: MAP-token-estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet), nimbus-map-usage.csv (csv)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus Health — continuous batching & $/1M token target

Quick internal — based on Aisha’s buckets we should propose: 
- Option A (Hosted, continuous-batching optimized): unit price at $620 / 1M tokens with auto-batching + soft latency targets; include a monthly spend cap and a 2-week rollback clause.
- Option B (Dedicated reserved): committed throughput with 20% lower $/1M (~$496 / 1M) but a 6–12 month commit and calendar-month reconciliation.

Also include quantization/latency appendix (use redwood-quant-profiles.pdf) showing expected p99 impacts at different quantization levels. I’ll draft the wording for the canary/fallback clause so we preserve UX during load spikes.

-Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@nimbushealth.com>, Tom Bradford <tom.bradford@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus Health — continuous batching & $/1M token target

Aisha / Tom — appreciation for the quick numbers and the attachments. Next steps from our side: 
1) We’ll send a two-option commercial proposal by end of day Thursday (Mar 18): Hosted (continuous-batching optimized) and Dedicated (reserved). Pricing will reflect the $600 target band you shared; we’ll show the blended $/1M and the committed-discount breakpoints.
2) We’ll include an appendix with expected latency profiles (p50/p95/p99) for the two options and the quantization tradeoffs (redwood-quant-profiles.pdf).
3) Please share the SOC2 questionnaire when ready — we’ll have our compliance packet available for you.
4) Can you confirm a 30-minute follow-up on Thursday (Mar 18) so we can walk the procurement team through the economics? I’m proposing 10:00am PT.

Attached: redwood-quant-profiles.pdf (estimator).

If the dates/times don’t work, send alternate windows and we’ll accommodate.

Best — Karthik

--
